The Grandest Game #1

The Grandest Game

Jennifer Lynn Barnes

3.94
88,351 ratings10,259 reviews
Rate this book
Goodreads Choice Award
Nominee for Readers' Favorite Young Adult Fiction (2024)
Seven tickets. An island of dreams. The chance of a lifetime.

Welcome to the Grandest Game, an annual competition run by billionaire Avery Grambs and the four infamous Hawthorne brothers, whose family fortune she inherited. Designed to give anyone a shot at fame and fortune, this year's game requires one of seven golden tickets to enter. With millions on the line, those seven players will do whatever it takes to win.
Some of the players are in it for the money. Some for power. Some for reasons all their own. Every single one of them has secrets. Amidst it all is Grayson Hawthorne, tasked with a vital role in this year's game. But as tensions rise and the mind-bending challenges push the players to their limits-physically, mentally, and emotionally-it soon becomes clear that not everyone is playing by the rules.

Jennifer Lynn Barnes delivers a brand-new series in the world of The Inheritance Games, where fan-favourite and new characters collide in a game you'll never forget.

Do you have what it takes to play?

About the author

Jennifer Lynn Barnes

58 books63.6k followers
Jennifer Lynn Barnes (who mostly goes by Jen) was born in Tulsa, Oklahoma. She has been, in turn, a competitive cheerleader, a volleyball player, a dancer, a debutante, a primate cognition researcher, a teen model, a comic book geek, and a lemur aficionado. She's been writing for as long as she can remember, finished her first full book (which she now refers to as a "practice book" and which none of you will ever see) when she was still in high school, and then wrote Golden the summer after her freshman year in college, when she was nineteen.

Jen graduated high school in 2002, and from Yale University with a degree in cognitive science (the study of the brain and thought) in May of 2006. She'll be spending the 2006-2007 school year abroad, doing autism research at the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom.

August 28, 2023
Before I start this review, please note that this is my honest opinion and if you find yourself disagreeing, please be respectful in the comments. I don't wish to be a ranter but I found things to be not working for me at all. It is a book that will work for others but I am absolutely unimpressed with it.

Firstly, the book is cunningly matketed or led to believe that the central character is Grayson. Even reading the blurb makes it seem like it's a spin off for him as a main character where we might get his pov. That's not the case tho. I found this marketing strategy to be false and just a way to get people hooked who wanted some justice to that particular character. The book's central figures are Rohan, Lyra and Gigi. Grayson yet again finds himself in a spot where he is underutilized imo.

The character dynamics don't work. Lyra has no personality. She is bland, no life to her. It's like reading a dead person's pov. Gigi is annoying. Rohan and Savannah kept things interesting at times but when they were next to other characters, their personalities clashed and it created an unbalance. This book was supposed to redeem Grayson's lack of personality, yet here we are. Idk what personal vendetta JLB has against a character she herself wrote but she clearly wants readers to not like him. The romance between him and Lyra is just not it. Avery and Jameson crumbs- the book could have used them more.

The plot is so weak. It's so effing weak, it's making me cry out of frustation. Also, correct me if am wrong but what's the point of Avery's games if only the rich people are participating? Like I don't mean to be a hater, but how is this book not a rich people making other rich people richer? 😭😂

The writing is average. It doesn't create the magic The Inheritance Games series did. The games and puzzles bored me. I just wanted it to end. The plot twists and reveals were bleh.

I believe it's time for me to part ways with this author and the future books in this series. An advice to authors- if you have wrapped up a popular series with a good end, let it stay that way. Don't go digging around and trying to create unnecessary books just for money grab. It backfires majority of the times. Not only was this book misleading in marketing, it was utter trash.


~•~•~
I swear if this one is half as bad as the last one, am out. Am here just for Grayson anyway...

⊹˚˖♟️⁺ ₊˚ 4 stars.

࿐ this review does not include spoilers.

plot.
‘the grandest game’ follows 7 characters as they compete to win the grandest game—an annual competition in which three guests are exclusively selected by the game master, avery kylie grambs, and four guests are lucky enough to score one of the seven golden tickets hidden around the world, which grants the fortunate individuals invites to the hawthorne island where the games will begin. each player has their reasons for participation; is it to prove themselves? is it for power? or is it simply for the 26 million dollar prize at the end of the tunnel? whatever it is, the players are suddenly launched into a world of puzzles, riddles, and games as they compete to win the grandest game with underlying danger and secrets lurking around the corner.


— ‘in the games that matter most, the only way to really play is to live.’


thoughts.
if i ever said anything about JLB milking the series, i take it back because i need the next book in my hands asap. this was such a page turner?? im gonna start off by saying that i am a complete sucker for anything set on an island, and the fact that there was a masquerade ball scene in this book makes me love it even more. i knew from the premise that i would love this, and the pacing of this book was so fast, i was hooked right from the get-go. the new characters were so refreshing, and 3 pov’s in this book were a great way to keep the reader engaged. there were times where the chapters ended on mini-cliffhangers, and i just wanted to skip the other pov’s because i was so eager to find things out. the narrative is so compelling, which isn’t something new with this author’s works. JLB is so good at making you YEARN to know what happens next in the story, and there was always something in the book that left me wondering. im not much of a detective, but i just kept trying to figure the riddles and puzzles out (to no avail) along with the many secrets and mysteries of the characters.

BUT, *cue the record scratch* this book is not perfect by any means. despite the great timing of action, gripping narrative, and fast paced plot, i did find a few faults which didnt sit right with me. there were alot of loose strings. the unfolding of lyra’s dad’s mystery was a very important aspect of the book. for something that was being built up since the first few pages, it sure was left in the dark at the end. it would have made so much more sense to wrap her mystery up in this book than potentially carry it out into the next book, since we already see great material to start the next book from. also, this is ostensibly the sort of book where events take place in a 24 hour timeline. however, the book is also pretty heavy in plot and mystery. because of this, the plot and romance felt quite rushed. linking back to the 3 pov’s topic, i would have liked this book to be longer because of the character density and the fact that this is told from multiple perspectives. it was as if she was given a strict limit as to how many pages to write, but i wouldnt have minded more pages at all!! i suppose there was an important plot twist in the book, but it was one that was previously revealed in the brothers hawthorne. but hey, atleast emily didnt come back to haunt the narrative for the 162717th time.


— ’ “the world just loves women who try.” odette caught gigi’s gaze and held it. “unless and until we try too hard.” ‘


characters & romance.

:: lyra & grayson ::
lyra is a very determined character, and her motivation was very selfless! she treats grayson like hes a piece of gum on the back of her shoe (deservedly) and i love it. i also loved the symbolism of the calla lily in relation to lyra. the fact that she was holding the flower in the same moments that she witnessed such a traumatic event as a child was so fascinating due to the flower’s symbolism to innocence, and the juxtaposition of her holding this symbolic flower as she loses her innocence was so well written. ive seen a couple arguments that grayson ’s character was bland here as opposed to in the inheritance games series, and i agree. i get that he had no reason to be cold towards lyra, since its not like she stole his inheritance or something, but still? where did grayson go? his name shouldve been plainson because thats what he was. plain. lyra described him as ‘sharp’ and whatever many times but its in response to him standing still? like he didnt even do anything in true grayson-fashion. however, their romance was still very cute and im very pleased that jennifer stopped torturing grayson and gave him his happy ending!!

:: rohan & savannah. ::
i dont read this genre, but rohan belongs in a dark romance book. i was lowkey struggling to pronounce his name (rowan? roe-han?) but he has that bad boy energy which i unfortunately love, and he was really smart. savannah is so fearless, i absolutely adore her intelligence and coldness. rohan and savannah were the best couple in this book i fear. its giving partners in crime. i started this book for grayson and lyra and abandoned them just as fast for these two. i mean the tension? i could taste it. however, the nicknames were foul. ‘british’ and ‘savvy’? get out. atleast gigi’s mimosa dude calls her ‘sunshine’, thats a beautiful nickname. but apart from that, they were my favs.

:: gigi. ::
gigi just deserves her own section. l-o-v-e her so much. she was so funny and kind. the quintessential sunshine girl. the fact that she was so determined to win and get a game ticket without intermediaries or advantages in the game was a great show of her dedication. at the end, we see her compare herself to her sister, whom she perceives as smarter than her. THIS BROKE ME. someone needs to tell this woman that she is good enough please. and the ending? im tweaking and need the next book in my hands right now.

conclusion.
for anyone in a slump, i highly recommend this!! despite some minor flaws, this book was really good. the narrative and pacing were nothing short of addictive, and im so excited for the next book which comes out in 2025!!

— ‘ “love is a strange and wild beast,” the old woman said. “it’s a gift and a comfort and a curse. remember that.” ‘

Jennifer Lynn Barnes has done it again 🧎🏻‍♀️🧎🏻‍♀️ Tbh I was a little worried going in knowing that there will be no og POV'S and I am so happy that I ended up absolutely loving it 🤭🤭 TGG can be read alone but I highly recommend reading the original trilogy and The Brothers Hawthorne first as characterwise it will make a lot more sense. I found the actual plot/mystery so interesting, and I was completely hooked 😍😍 In the first 4 books if I'm being honest I kinda would jst follow the plot and never rly have any suspicions of what might happen next but in TGG I had so many theories 🤔🤔 and to my surprise I actually guessed some of the riddles 😃😃 Another thing I loved was all the subtle mentions to the previous books, it jst made me so happy 🥰🥰 And the cliffhanger OMG Jennifer what did you do 😭😭

.ೃ࿐⁀➷ Characters

❥ Gigi: I love Gigi so so so much 😍😍 she is my spirit animal fr 🤭🤭 She is so fun and bubbly despite everything she has gone through 🥺🥺 Her quotes throughout the book, I was highlighting like a mad woman 🫣🫣 And the way she wanted to make sure that Brady got enough money to take care of him mum regardless of if he won was jst so sweet of her 😭😭 My new mantra is in a world of Eve's be a Gigi ❤️❤️ Also is it bad that I'm still shipping her with Slade 🫣🫣

❥ Lyra: I have been impatiently waiting for Lyra to make an appearance since the second she was introduced in The Brothers Hawthorne, but no one could have prepared me for how much I love her 🤭🤭 She is so sarcastic and witty and literally everything I could ever want in a fmc 🥰🥰 I also felt like I could relate to her I could see so much of myself in her (idk whether that's a good or bad thing 😂😂) Some the things that we learnt abt her past almost had me in tears and all I wanted to do was give her a huge hug 😭😭🫂🫂

❥ Rohan: Tbh I didn't go into TGG expecting to like Rohan and I certainly didn't expect to come out of it loving him 🤭🤭 I loved his character arc and learning abt his past (even tho it made me want to cry 😭😭) Idk why I originally thought that he would be terrible at solving all the riddles and his only talent was gambling (what was I thinking 🤦‍♀️🤦‍♀️) so I was pleasantly surprised by every choice he made and how clever/cunning it was 😂😂 And his banter with Savanah was just 🤌🤌 I can't wait to get more of him in Glorious Rivals ❤️❤️

❥ The Hawthornes + Avery: Grayson and I have a rocky past to say the least but for some reason I actually felt for him and could connect with his struggles 🥺🥺 I wish we got more time with Jameson and Avery and how they chose/found Odette and Knox and I also wish we got more of Xander (when am I not wishing that 😂😂) and what role he had in the making of the game. Also, OMG the reveal abt I'm so happy for Libby and Nash ❤️❤️

❥ Other Characters: I have so many mixed opinions on the other characters 🤔🤔 Kane kinda annoyed me tbh but then again when you learnt abt his backstory I felt so so bad for him 🥺🥺 Brady, it's safe to say was not a plot twist that I was expecting, so that hurt 😭😭 Calla *cough Emily 2.0 cough* need I say any more 🙄🙄 I did like Savannah but pls don't continue your plan for revenge 😭😭 And I was SO SO SO sure that Odette was and I mean I guess I was pretty close but still 🥲🥲

❥ Savannah + Rohan: SCREAMINGGG I love these two sm 🫠🫠 Before going into the Grandest Game I did have my predictions that perhaps we were going to get a romance between these two and I'm SO HAPPY I was right 😩😩 Their banter is EVERYTHING 😭😭 And the way Rohan would call Savannah Savvy was so cute 🤭🤭

"𝑺𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒑𝒆𝒐𝒑𝒍𝒆 𝒄𝒂𝒏 𝒎𝒂𝒌𝒆 𝒎𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒌𝒆𝒔, 𝒎𝒂𝒌𝒆 𝒂𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒅𝒔, 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒎𝒐𝒗𝒆 𝒐𝒏. 𝑨𝒏𝒅 𝒔𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒐𝒇 𝒖𝒔 𝒍𝒊𝒗𝒆 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉 𝒆𝒂𝒄𝒉 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚 𝒎𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒌𝒆 𝒘𝒆 𝒎𝒂𝒌𝒆 𝒄𝒂𝒓𝒗𝒆𝒅 𝒊𝒏𝒕𝒐 𝒖𝒔, 𝒊𝒏𝒕𝒐 𝒉𝒐𝒍𝒍𝒐𝒘 𝒑𝒍𝒂𝒄𝒆𝒔 𝒘𝒆 𝒅𝒐𝒏'𝒕 𝒌𝒏𝒐𝒘 𝒉𝒐𝒘 𝒕𝒐 𝒇𝒊𝒍𝒍."

Dear Jennifer, I'm aware you love torturing us, but ending a book on such a cliffhanger should be illegal. How on earth am I supposed to wait ONE YEAR for Glorious Rivals? I need that book for yesterday.

"𝑰 𝒉𝒂𝒗𝒆 𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒏𝒕 𝒎𝒚 𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒊𝒓𝒆 𝒍𝒊𝒇𝒆 𝒃𝒆𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒇𝒊𝒏𝒆 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒏 𝑰 𝒘𝒂𝒔𝒏'𝒕. 𝑰 𝒌𝒏𝒐𝒘 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒑𝒓𝒊𝒄𝒆. 𝑰 𝒌𝒏𝒐𝒘 𝒘𝒉𝒂𝒕 𝒊𝒕'𝒔 𝒍𝒊𝒌𝒆 𝒕𝒐 𝒃𝒆𝒂𝒓 𝒕𝒉𝒂𝒕 𝒑𝒓𝒊𝒏𝒄𝒆 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉 𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚 𝒄𝒆𝒍𝒍 𝒊𝒏 𝒚𝒐𝒖𝒓 𝒃𝒐𝒅𝒚. 𝑰𝒕 𝒊𝒔𝒏'𝒕 𝒘𝒐𝒓𝒕𝒉 𝒊𝒕."

At first I was kinda bored, but when the game began, I got really invested. What I love the most about JLB's books is that they're fast paced, and chapters in them are short, which makes you just speed through these books. The riddles and puzzles were interesting, and I really liked the way they were being solved.

"𝑺𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒕𝒊𝒎𝒆𝒔, 𝒊𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒈𝒂𝒎𝒆𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒂𝒕 𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒓 𝒎𝒐𝒔𝒕, 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒐𝒏𝒍𝒚 𝒘𝒂𝒚 𝒕𝒐 𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒚 𝒑𝒍𝒂𝒚 𝒊𝒔 𝒕𝒐 𝒍𝒊𝒗𝒆."

If it comes to three povs we got, I have to admit that I enjoyed Lyra's one the most! I sorta didn't care about Gigi's pov, though. I mean, it wasn't bad, but simply it didn't seem as interesting as Lyra and Rohan's did?

"𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒅𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒆𝒓 𝒐𝒇 𝒕𝒐𝒖𝒄𝒉 𝒊𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒄𝒓𝒖𝒆𝒍 𝒃𝒆𝒂𝒖𝒕𝒚 𝒐𝒇 𝒂 𝒎𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕 𝒈𝒐𝒏𝒆 𝒕𝒐𝒐 𝒇𝒂𝒔𝒕 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒃𝒖𝒓𝒏𝒆𝒅 𝒊𝒏𝒕𝒐 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒌𝒊𝒏."

Frankly, I have never liked Gray for some unexplainable reasons. It had always been that way. So it's funny, how people say that Gray is bland here opposite to other books, but for me it's the book that made me like him. It took me five books to like him, so we really had a slow burn thing going on. He may seem different, but it's Gray who's finally in his healing process, who started to express his emotions and worked up the courage to let people in. Thankfully, JLB stopped torturing him. Oh man, the phone girl & a Hawthorne boy delivered. I loved Lyra & Gray's dynamic. I mean, the forehead scene, the chandelier scene, the panic attack scene, the scene in which he called her "sweetheart"(I almost died) I ate every of these scenes up and left no crumbs. I genuinely adored every scene with Lyra and Gray. Istg, Jameson and Avery were lowkey shipping them. They knew what they were doing when they told them to draw each other in order to earn a hint.

"𝑯𝒆 𝒌𝒏𝒆𝒘 𝒘𝒉𝒂𝒕 𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒎𝒆𝒂𝒏𝒕 𝒕𝒐 𝒉𝒆𝒓. 𝑯𝒆 𝒌𝒏𝒆𝒘, 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒇𝒓𝒐𝒎 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒍𝒐𝒐𝒌 𝒊𝒏 𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒆𝒚𝒆𝒔, 𝒔𝒉𝒆 𝒘𝒐𝒖𝒍𝒅 𝒉𝒂𝒗𝒆 𝒔𝒘𝒐𝒓𝒏 𝒊𝒕 𝒎𝒆𝒂𝒏𝒕 𝒔𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒕𝒐 𝒉𝒊𝒎 𝒕𝒐𝒐."

"𝑳𝒂𝒔𝒕 𝒚𝒆𝒂𝒓, 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒏 𝑰 𝒕𝒐𝒍𝒅 𝒚𝒐𝒖 𝒕𝒐 𝒔𝒕𝒐𝒑 𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈—𝑰 𝒅𝒊𝒅𝒏'𝒕 𝒎𝒆𝒂𝒏 𝒊𝒕."

"𝒀𝒐𝒖 𝒘𝒊𝒍𝒍 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒃𝒂𝒄𝒌 𝒕𝒐 𝒎𝒆, 𝒐𝒓 𝑰 𝒘𝒊𝒍𝒍 𝒎𝒂𝒌𝒆 𝒚𝒐𝒖 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒃𝒂𝒄𝒌 𝒕𝒐 𝒎𝒆."

I liked Savannah and Rohan too. I loved how he was calling her Savvy. Savannah's nickname for Rohan was terrible, though. I mean "British", seriously? Istg, he was giving off dark romance vibes in some scenes, like in the scene in which he took the knife to the shower? Yeah, that didn't feel like he belonged to a YA book. When Savannah told Rohan that Avery killed her father, I was like, no, girl, she did not, actually, it was your father who wanted to kill Avery, so you definitely have a bad source of information.

"𝑰 𝒔𝒆𝒆 𝒚𝒐𝒖, 𝑺𝒂𝒗𝒂𝒏𝒏𝒂𝒉. 𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒍 𝒚𝒐𝒖. 𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒓𝒚 𝒚𝒐𝒖. 𝑭𝒊𝒓𝒆, 𝒏𝒐𝒕 𝒊𝒄𝒆."

"𝑬𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒓𝒔, 𝑺𝒂𝒗𝒗𝒚—𝒖𝒏𝒕𝒊𝒍 𝒏𝒐𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒅𝒐𝒆𝒔."

I was so happy when Jameson, Nash, Xander or Avery made an appearance. I missed the Hawthornes, and the Hawthorne's heiress. I loved all of the averyjameson crumbs.They made my heart so full. 🥹🤍

"𝑩𝒆𝒔𝒊𝒅𝒆 𝑨𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚, 𝑱𝒂𝒎𝒆𝒔𝒐𝒏 𝒘𝒂𝒔 𝒍𝒐𝒐𝒌𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂𝒕 𝒉𝒆𝒓 𝒍𝒊𝒌𝒆 𝒔𝒉𝒆 𝒘𝒂𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒖𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒎𝒐𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒓𝒔 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒆𝒕𝒆𝒓𝒏𝒊𝒕𝒚, 𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝒓𝒐𝒍𝒍𝒆𝒅 𝒊𝒏𝒕𝒐 𝒐𝒏𝒆."

coming back after finishing the last book of the series to tell you that this spin-off IS NOT optional if you don't want to be left in the dark as a reader of the original inheritance games series.
____

spoiler-free (but contains spoilers for the original trilogy)

i want to put out a disclaimer before i start: this review is definitely not coming from a neutral standpoint since i absolutely hated how jennifer lynn barnes let the original trilogy play out (aka what she did to grayson). i could write a whole thesis about the bad decisions that were made and the way grayson was wronged. i haven’t fully reviewed the original trilogy because i know that it will be LOADED – but i will get to it hopefully someday.

on a different note first up: the audiobook was a 10/10, highly recommend (if you want a story that delivers absolutely nothing!)

let's start:

general:

this book was strategically marketed a way that made us readers believe it’s going to feature grayson as the main character (spoiler: it’s not). it was just a way to fish the grayson stans who just want him to get the happy ending he deserves. the chance for this was already given at the novella 'the brothers hawthorne' but was not used ofc. so here we are. and what can i say? i am just absolutely sick of him constantly being stepped on and his trauma utilised for the plot (in the original trilogy and here) only to not be dealt with properly. he deserves so so much better. but well, why don’t we throw in a dozen new characters (yes, i know it’s a series of its own and will therefore contain new characters – but still) and give them complex backstories to deal with instead of focusing on graysons! i guess you’d need grayson stans to keep buying the books to make sales right? cash grab at its finest.

oh and btw, you can absolutely NOT read this separately from the original trilogy – even if jlb tries to sell it as such. nothing gets explained so you will basically be thrown into open water if you decide to read this first (what i don't even expect anyone to do since we're all just here for the og characters).


plot:

the grandest games don't make any sense. it's literally just a way for my not at all selfish girl avery to waste her time designing useless games. imagine hosting games with a price money of over 20 million dollars and not expecting people to betray their whole family tree over it. 'everyone should be able to play and find themselves through these games!' – girl nobody cares about these cringy riddles if you're putting 20 million dollars at stake!! crazy.



oh and the riddles were mid. not just because i only cared about grayson – they were truly underwhelming.

the so called plot-twist was meh. foreshadowed in the brothers hawthorne already. don't care, next.


characters and their dynamics:

as you'd think given what i wrote above: this did nothing for grayson. we were introduced to phone girl – lyra, who is his love interest. but oh! her character (her backstory) doesn‘t have much complexity - just like my girl bravery!
this obviously isn’t a result of jlb’s weak character building since the hawthornes and all the other characters are complex, so i really don't understand what her problem is. why stop at lyra and avery? i just don’t get it.
but well, at this point i only have the option of gaslighting myself into shipping lyra and grayson.. it’s not that i don’t like them together at all– but they and their chemistry seemed rushed and forced.




writing:

getting into this, i couldn’t help but notice that the writing was pretty bad. the more i read, i realized that it’s because it's written in third-person perspective (compared to the original trilogy). the brother’s hawthorne was too, but this seemed to be worse for some reason. third-person clearly isn’t jlb’s strong suit.

and while it obviously varies from person to person, i found the imagery hard with this one (which i also noticed in the og trilogy, but not as severe). someone please tell jlb that not everyone can picture a roblox ballroom with upside-down archways floating above the floor that change directions.

_

well, what can i say? i'm so disappointed but not surprised. i will continue reading this series because i care so much about grayson, but just know that i'm not happy at all.

ꕀꕀꕀꕀꕀꕀ

I have mixed feelings about this book. I enjoyed the riddles, the mystery and the setting, but I didn’t like most of the characters, the character development was lacking and the pacing was uneven. I liked trying to solve the riddles and puzzles. The setting was fun and I liked the escape room aspect of the game. The writing was engaging and easy to follow. The characters were a disappointing part to me. I really like Xander and Grayson, but I didn’t like most of the other main characters. I also didn’t feel a connection to many of the main characters and the character development was lacking. Gigi was an okay character I liked her better than the other characters she is brave and not arrogant. Savannah, Rohan, and Knox were all arrogant and all they cared about was wining. Knox’s character felt very flat and his past was rarely explored. I wasn’t a fan of Lyra because she judged and was rude to Grayson without knowing anything about him. I wish all of the characters past were explored in more depth. I liked the interactions with the characters from the Inheritance Games especially Xander, Grayson and Jameson. The ending was underwhelming and confusing. Overall this was an okay book for me, the riddles and puzzles were fun, but the characters were disappointing and the character development was lacking.
